title: Spring Onion Cornmeal Waffles
changes_from_base: Mostly fine white cornmeal with dark brown sugar, chilli flakes, olive oil and buttermilk, studded with spring onion pieces; whole eggs, no whisked whites, served sweet-and-savoury with maple syrup, jam and butter.
summary: Savoury-sweet cornmeal waffles flecked with spring onion and a touch of chilli, finished with maple syrup and jam.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
spring onions, cut on an angle into 2 cm pieces
oil spray for the iron, as needed

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 140 g cornmeal, 65 g plain flour, 2 tbsp dark brown sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ¼ tsp chilli flakes and ⅛ tsp salt together in a large bowl.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Beat 2 eggs well, then stir in 320 ml buttermilk, the sliced spring onions and 1 tbsp olive oil, and pour this into the dry mix, whisking to combine.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and spray lightly if needed.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Ladle in about 180 ml batter and cook until cooked through and golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Move the cooked waffles to a tray and serve warm with maple syrup, a dusting of icing sugar, and a little berry jam and butter.

tips: Cut the spring onions on an angle into 2 cm pieces so every bite gets a little.
Dust the icing sugar through a tea strainer for an even, light covering rather than clumps.
These waffles reheat well, so they're a good one to make ahead and freeze.
storage: The waffles can be made ahead, cooled and frozen, then reheated in a 200 °C oven for 5 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
